The stage on one page how a case moves through it, its outcomes, what is at stake

An online store selling outdoor clothing and equipment to signed-in customers through a web front end (and a mobile app), with orders accepted, stock-checked, paid and shipped by back-end services joined by a message broker. Configuration described: the Aspire AppHost as deployed to Azure Container Apps, with UseFoundry=true so the chat and embedding models are present; Postgres, RabbitMQ and Redis run as the application's own containers. proposed: no source says which configuration runs in production; this is the fullest the repository defines. In this configuration the services run outside Development, so /health is not mapped and logs default to Information.

Expected of the stage. A case that enters it leaves within the promise (proposed: none assumed by the code; the carrier's delivery commitment would set one), in one of these ways:

What is at stake.

  • Order id ("Id"): The only key that joins the order across services and to the customer
  • Order total (sum of Units x UnitPrice): Money the customer pays; value blocked while the order is stuck
  • Items and units (ordering."orderItems"): What must be in stock and shipped
  • Buyer (ordering.buyers "IdentityGuid"): Who is waiting and who is told
  • Delivery address: Where the goods must arrive
  • Payment method (card number masked to the last four digits): What is charged

Runbook: Deliver the order › Alert

Shipped orders not confirmed delivered within the stage's promise

A shipped order not delivered within the stage's promise leaves the customer without the goods they expect (flows.csv the flow “Fulfilling a customer's order”, delivers). The record this alert needs does not exist yet: the code records nothing after Shipped, so a per-order delivery confirmation must be added before it can fire. The bound is the stage's promise, which no source states (stages.csv the stage “Deliver the order”, proposed:). Its runbook entry has no tests, and that is the finding, not an omission: tests come from the failures of the move a stage's cases wait on, and these wait on delivery, which no part of the application carries out. The stage's one recorded move, “Webhook subscribers are told the order is shipped”, tells webhook subscribers and does not move an order. Its cases go to the carrier, outside this runbook, until a delivery move and its record are added

This measure is not emitted yet; deployed as written, the alert fires on No data until it is.

It has been above the operators’ threshold for longer than their window (the alert).

Its cases those held in the stage past the bound. A case not past the bound is not one of this alert's.
Look back from when the oldest of its cases entered the stage, to now. The alert fires only once a case has waited past the bound, so its cause can be as old as that: never read a test over only the time since the count began rising.
Do now
  1. List its cases and set the look-back. Every check below runs on these cases, over that time. List them with the alert’s own count:
    How
    per order, the time since its OrderStatusChangedToShipped outbox row "CreationTime" with no delivery confirmation for it; needs a per-order delivery record (a carrier's confirmation) the code does not keep: the last state is Shipped
  2. Contain. No hold is needed: the cases the alert counts are still in the stage, and nothing more is done to them while they wait.
  3. Do not: the register names no action to avoid here.
  4. Escalate or declare as soon as a trigger is met, at any point below. Triggers ›
Check first
1Is this already known?
How
Look for an open incident, or a known error with a fix in flight, for any of these parts: Ordering API, Webhooks API, Webhooks database, Event bus, Webhook subscriber endpoint. Not the cause if there is none; the cause if one is open: link it and close.
Yes → Already known
2Was it planned?
How
Look for a maintenance window on any of those parts, or a planned change to a timing the stage depends on (Each post is bounded only by the standard resilience handler every HTTP client carries: each attempt 10 seconds, up to 3 retries, 30 seconds in all; the posts to all subscriptions go out together and are awaited together. No clock watches the message waiting in queue Webhooks). Not the cause if there is none; the cause if a window is open or a setting was changed on purpose: link it and close.
Yes → Planned change
3Did something change when it started?
How
Look for any deploy, configuration change or unplanned restart of those parts since the look-back time above. Not the cause if there is none; the cause if a change lines up with the start.
Yes → Roll the change back, or escalate to the owner of the part that changed
4Is it already recovering?
How
Read the alert's own count over one window (for a count of cases waiting, with the oldest only just past the bound). Not the cause if it is not falling; it is recovering if the count falls within one window: confirm it is back under its threshold, then close.
Yes → Self-healed
Find the cause

No record to count: Tests come from the failures of the move a stage's cases wait on, and these wait on delivery, which no part of the application carries out: the code's last state is Shipped.
